messages:

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Netflow & backout criteria: private cluster maintenance window (proposal)

Hi Lydia / FinCorp NetOps team,

Per our onboarding call, we're planning a maintenance window for your private deployment (VPC-connected cluster) to apply security patches and a targeted runtime upgrade. The goal is to keep the cluster pinned to the current model-serving artifact if we detect any quality regressions but still apply OS/GPU driver security fixes.

Proposed window:
- Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026
- Start: 02:00 UTC / 19:00 PDT (Wed, 30 Sep)
- Expected duration: 2 hours (30 min canary + rolling restarts + verification)

High-level plan (attached: private-maintenance-playbook-v1.4.pdf):
- Pre-checks: netflow baseline (netflow-checksheet-2026-09.csv), LB health, node-level telemetry snapshot
- Canary: 10% traffic routed to canary instances pinned to artifact v2.3.1-quant (no model delta)
- Roll: rolling node restarts with KV cache warmup and automatic prefix cache replay disabled briefly
- Verification: end-to-end p99 latency and error-rate thresholds (see playbook)
- Backout criteria (proposed):
  - Request error-rate increase > 1.5x baseline for > 10 min OR
  - p99 latency regress > 300ms absolute increase for > 10 min OR
  - Model quality regress on spot-check prompts (failing test set)

Ask:
1) Confirm maintenance window or propose alternate date/time.
2) Confirm FinCorp can run the netflow checklist during pre-check (attachment).
3) Provide emergency access approval (DocuSign link will follow) if your ops team requires break-glass keys for rollback.

I'll kick off a Jira INF-4827 to track tasks and DM you the DocuSign link once we confirm scheduling.

Thanks,
Sofia

Subject: Re: Netflow & backout criteria: private cluster maintenance window (proposal)

Sofia,

Thanks for the draft. A couple of technical clarifications from the runtime/serving side:
- Version pinning: we should pin the model-serving artifact but allow driver-level updates only if the kernel change path is ABI compatible with our optimized kernels. I propose we pin to v2.3.1-quant and deploy a separate driver package flagged as "security-only" with a no-op model reload.
- KV cache: during rolling restarts, set cache-warmup window to 5 minutes instead of immediate replay to avoid request bursts. We should also drain in-flight long-lived streaming sessions before rebooting nodes.

I'll add specific command snippets to INF-4827. Dev / Mina, please confirm the health-check endpoints and the drain sequence are covered.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick follow-up with concrete rollback/playbook items we must agree on before scheduling:
1) Canary rollback: If canary fails, traffic should fail back to existing instances and we must automatically mark canary instances unhealthy in the LB. Canary rollback must be complete within 15 minutes.
2) Full backout: If rollback is triggered during a roll, the automation should stop new node restarts and run the rollback-scripts-list.txt to restore pinned artifact and warm caches from snapshots. Target restore RTO: 30 minutes.
3) Telemetry gates: control-plane must verify
   - avg error-rate <= 1.2x baseline AND
   - p99 latency <= baseline + 250ms AND
   - no >5% sample failing synthetic prompts in the quick-eval suite
4) Network gating: FinCorp NetOps to confirm netflow shows no unusual SYN/RETRAN spikes and BGP sessions stable. If MTU adjustments are part of the patch, those must be coordinated earlier in a separate maintenance.

I've attached a trimmed netflow-checksheet and the rollback script index. I'll create the runbook checklist in INF-4827 for sign-offs.

-Dev

- Can you confirm you will not change MTU or BGP during this window? (we had a bad incident last year when MTU changed mid-maintenance)

Also, please send the DocuSign emergency access form so our security team can approve break-glass access in advance. If everything looks good we'll sign and return within 24 hours.
